question: Explain the link between financial policy and corporate strategy, and the main areas where financial decisions support strategic planning.
sources: ICAI CA Final syllabus (2023 scheme), Paper 2 AFM: Financial Policy and Corporate Strategy
Generally accepted corporate finance principles on investment, financing and dividend decisions

points.label: Why they are linked
points.description: Strategy sets where the business wants to go; financial policy decides how resources are raised and used to get there, so a strategy is only workable if it can be financed at an acceptable risk and cost.
points.basis: Corporate finance principle: strategy and finance must be planned together

points.label: Investment decisions
points.description: Capital is allocated to projects, products and markets that fit the chosen strategy and earn more than the cost of capital.
points.basis: Corporate finance principle: capital allocation to value-creating projects

points.label: Financing decisions
points.description: Choosing the mix of debt and equity and the sources of funds, balancing cost, control, flexibility and financial risk to suit the strategy.
points.basis: Corporate finance principle: capital structure and sources of finance

points.label: Dividend and retention decisions
points.description: How much profit to pay out and how much to retain for growth, keeping shareholder expectations and future funding needs in balance.

points.label: Balancing goals and risk
points.description: Financial planning balances liquidity, profitability and risk, and the goals of different stakeholders, with value maximisation as the guiding objective; plans are reviewed as conditions change.
points.basis: Corporate finance principle: wealth maximisation and balancing financial goals
